boundary: A fictional expedition, informed by real observations. Game resource units and the seven-shift schedule are training rules. Game exposure is not a medical dose. The storm is a labelled September 2017 historical replay; Aurora's expedition is in April 2046. The shift-4 Earth-link cutoff is an authored training event, not a computed Earth-set.

tradeoffs.title: Power and air
tradeoffs.predict: Could daylight power pay for air before darkness?
tradeoffs.why: Charging is capped before systems spend energy. Producing air in daylight can use energy that would otherwise overflow. Exactly zero energy is an empty battery; only an unpaid demand causes a blackout.

tradeoffs.title: Shelter and garden water
tradeoffs.predict: When could borrowed water return to Alo?
tradeoffs.why: The wall and the garden share a reservoir. Water in the wall helps shield the crew, but a wall holding at least 4 leaves the garden thirsty. Storm exposure resolves before an ordinary drain; crate shielding is separate from water.

tradeoffs.title: Historical evidence and the scenario
tradeoffs.predict: Which readings were measured, and which came from the training model?
tradeoffs.why: The proton observations and historical event record inform the exercise. The station, its resource costs and its night schedule are authored. Computed viewing geometry does not turn the shift-4 link cutoff into an observed event.

options: Use charging energy before it overflows
Plants instantly make all the crew's air
Darkness removes the need for air
questions.explanation: Daylight charging can overflow the battery. The air maker can use some of that available energy to build a reserve.

questions.prompt: Why can shelter water hurt Alo?
options: The wall borrows water from the garden reservoir
questions.explanation: The wall and garden share water. Return it after the exposure step it was protecting; crates provide separate shielding.

questions.prompt: Which label means a real measurement?
questions.explanation: Observed identifies a measured record. Computed geometry and simulated game resource units have different labels.
